that dot also carries the centre column, i.e. the bottom of R5 above and V-DC(one port) 22 below. Judgment calls: (a) Resistor 16 and V-DC(one port) 20 are BOTH off-frame (bbox centres at y=-21.5 and y=-16.6, above the top edge). Exactly two wires leave the top edge: the ground rail at x~86 and the base lead of PNP 8 at x~207. R16 spans x=124..159 off-frame, i.e. squarely between those two stubs, so it is read as bridging them (0 -- n1); V-DC 20 spans x=206..226, sitting directly over the x~207 stub, so its single terminal is n1. This is the only reading that leaves no terminal dangling. (b) The y~288 horizontal is drawn with a clear downward DIP at x~137 where the n8 column passes: at 12x the column continues below the dip, so this is a crossover hop, NOT a junction - R17's left end reaches the ground rail instead. (c) The diode-string horizontal at y~395 makes the same kind of dip at x~295..305 where the centre (R5/V-DC22) column passes; no dot, and joining them would short Diode 0, so it is a crossover. By contrast the crossing at (305,448) carries an unmistakable ink blob and IS a junction. (d) Left end of the y~288 horizontal: the ground rail's stroke stops at exactly y=288 with a rightward hook and the horizontal restarts ~2px later. Read as a T-junction (pen skip), since otherwise R17's left terminal would dangle. (e) BJT pin readings from the emitter arrowheads at 14x: NPN 3, 4, 9, 11, 13 all have the arrow on the lead that runs toward the ground rail / lower node (that lead = emitter); PNP 2, 8, 10, 12 have the arrow pointing INTO the base bar on the lead listed as emitter. All nine BJTs are drawn rotated, with a horizontal base bar and the base lead entering vertically. (f) All long straight runs in this drawing (both vertical rails, the x~137 and x~300 columns) render as dash-dot after preprocessing; they were checked at high zoom and are single continuous conductors. (g) Diode terminal order is listed as drawn (both diodes point left: bar/cathode on the left, triangle base/anode on the right); 2-terminal order does not affect any metric.
